title: Training compute and energy cost scaling
bottleneck: Each frontier generation costs roughly an order of magnitude more than the last — training runs now exceed $100M — while performance gains per dollar shrink. Power is becoming the binding constraint: data centers need gigawatts that grids can't provision quickly, and the environmental cost of training is rising as a political issue. The economics of scaling are deteriorating even as the strategy continues.
why_it_blocks: If each capability step costs 10x more for diminishing returns, AI progress becomes affordable only to a handful of actors — and eventually uneconomical for everyone. Rising costs also concentrate research in a few labs, narrowing who gets to push the frontier forward.
current_state: Labs build dedicated power plants and chase efficiency; algorithmic gains partially offset costs, but the exponential cost curve hasn't bent.
